verifierBody:
pstack-verifier: PASS+NOTES @ 7dc0ff0fb0f09d7d966f2abce10594a26a10c7b5

Verified by DeepSeek (deepseek-flash), a different model family from the author, on a GitHub-hosted runner. It read the diff and text evidence only, never screenshots.

The diff adds a per-table expand button and a sheet that reuses the existing markdown table renderer with a title from the nearest preceding heading, and it builds, but no driven journey touched the new button or sheet. The only driven journey, session-reader.md, passed identically on parent and head, so it shows no regression in the chat flow but says nothing about the new feature, and the added unit tests were never run.

Journeys driven (parent is the app before this change, head is after):
- `session-reader.md` parent: passed, head: passed

Evidence:
- Journey session-reader.md passed on both parent and head (driver exit 0, receipts VERIFY_SENT_528/VERIFY_ENTER_528/VERIFY_INTERRUPTED_528), so chat sign-in, send and interrupt flows show no regression from this change.
- The head side's build-apk and build-instrumentation steps succeeded, so the production code in the diff compiles even though no Gradle run happened on the author's machine.
- The session-reader artifact steps are only sign-in, host-key, sessions, attach menu, send draft/result and interrupt; none of them opens a table sheet or clicks a table expand button.
- The description states the new ChatTableExpandTest and the added DesignKitTest expandButton check were not run, and no unit-test output appears in the evidence for either side.
- ChatTableExpandTest asserts the button count, sheet width, single-line long cell and Close behaviour, but as an unrunnable-here unit test it is not evidence of the on-device behaviour.

Not covered:
- The expand button being present on every chat table and absent on prose, as seen on a device
- Opening the table sheet with a dark chat backdrop behind it, and the preceding heading becoming the sheet title
- Scrolling the sheet up, down and sideways and a long cell staying on one line instead of wrapping
- Closing the sheet with the X button, a drag down, a tap outside or the system back button, and the chat staying where it was
- How a small chat table looks with the 32dp button overlaid on its top-right corner, which could sit over the last column header
- The new unit tests (ChatTableExpandTest, DesignKitTest.expandButtonIsASmallRoundSurfaceControl) actually passing, since no Gradle or test run is in the evidence

Run: https://github.com/valentinyeo/multiprompt-android/actions/runs/43763176155
